title: BM25 field-weight tuning
approach: Retuned title, body, and label weights on a 120-query slice.
outcome: Overall recall rose two points, but cross-team blocker recall was unchanged.
lesson: Generic lexical tuning is an established baseline, not a sufficient new direction.

title: Always-on cross-encoder reranking
approach: Reranked every query with the current cross-encoder.
outcome: Recall improved four points while p95 latency rose above 700 ms.
lesson: The expensive component may need selective use rather than further scaling.

title: Title-only dense embeddings
approach: Replaced lexical title matching with local dense embeddings.
outcome: Paraphrase matches improved, but ownership and linked blocker tickets remained absent.
lesson: Semantic similarity alone does not recover relational evidence.

title: Remote LLM query rewriting
approach: Prototyped external model calls for symptom paraphrases.
outcome: The prototype was stopped before evaluation because private incident text could not leave the environment.
lesson: A proposal that depends on a remote model is infeasible for this pilot.

title: Ungated two-hop graph expansion
approach: Expanded candidates through ticket links and service ownership edges.
outcome: Cross-team recall improved, but stale links produced wrong-owner results and candidate explosion.
lesson: Relationships are promising only if freshness and path quality are controlled.

title: Post-retrieval access filtering
approach: Retrieved broadly, then removed results the requester could not view.
outcome: No private text was displayed, but authorized result quality varied when labels were missing.
lesson: Permission handling affects candidate generation as well as display filtering.

title: Confidence-only explanations
approach: Added high, medium, or low confidence badges to each result.
outcome: Operators interpreted high confidence as a completeness guarantee and trust fell after misses.
lesson: Explanations should expose evidence paths or uncertainty causes, not unsupported confidence.

title: Manual service alias dictionary
approach: Added aliases for twelve recently renamed services.
outcome: Rename queries improved, but the hand-maintained list became stale within weeks.
lesson: Alias normalization helps, but maintenance and temporal drift need study.

title: Duplicate result collapse
approach: Collapsed tickets with identical normalized titles.
outcome: Visible duplication fell while cloned templates from unrelated services were sometimes merged.
lesson: Duplicate handling needs service and relationship context.

title: Owner metadata completion sprint
approach: Filled missing owner fields for the highest-volume services.
outcome: Owner coverage improved locally, but responsibility transfers still invalidated older tickets.
lesson: Static cleanup does not solve ownership change over time.

title: Large reranker fine-tuning
approach: Estimated a fine-tuning run on a larger reranker.
outcome: The minimum useful run exceeded the current GPU and engineering budget.
lesson: The two-week pilot needs a smaller or training-free approach.

title: Ticket summary snippets
approach: Generated short summaries before applying final display filters.
outcome: Summaries occasionally preserved phrases from restricted comments after the source ticket was withheld.
lesson: Derived text must obey the same access boundary as source text.

title: Same-team personalization
approach: Boosted the requester's own service and team history.
outcome: Same-team recall increased while cross-team blocker discovery declined.
lesson: Personalization can deepen the exact boundary the new study should address.

title: Weekly relationship-index refresh
approach: Rebuilt ownership and link features once per week.
outcome: The index was cheap to operate but wrong-owner paths persisted between transfers and refreshes.
lesson: Freshness policy may matter more than raw refresh throughput.

title: Mandatory human escalation
approach: Sent every low-score query to a service desk analyst.
outcome: Accuracy improved, but median incident response slowed by nineteen minutes.
lesson: Human review should target informative slices, not sit in the online path.

title: Metadata-only lightweight baseline
approach: Combined lexical scores with service, age, and ownership metadata.
outcome: It nearly matched the cross-encoder on short same-team queries at one fifth the latency.
lesson: Any complex proposal should beat a carefully tuned simple baseline on the slice it targets.
